note: Why the gateway process stopped, said in the one way that survives the process boundary. launchd reports the exit code of the service it supervises, and the desktop host reads it back from `launchctl print` to tell someone why their background service is not starting. The server owns the mapping from its own fatal errors to these numbers and the host owns the sentence each one becomes; this file is the contract between them, and neither side reads the other's log to guess. 1 stays the unclassified failure, so a build that has not been taught a new reason still exits non-zero and is reported as a service that will not start. A failure that starting again cannot fix is the one case this channel cannot carry: launchd's only exit condition is `KeepAlive: { SuccessfulExit: false }`, so such a run exits zero to stop the relaunch loop and writes its reason — a name from this table — into `logs/gateway-startup-failure.json`, which the host reads when the exit status has nothing to say. One number here is not a failure at all: `stoppedOnRequest` is what the supervised gateway exits with when it served and was asked to stop, because zero would tell launchd to leave it stopped and being asked to stop is not being told to stay stopped. `launchctl bootout` unloads the job before that status is read, so the service that is meant to stop still stops.
